records.body: PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Source: Dependency/licensing notes (marked open there, not in the Open decisions list). Recommendation: a permissive FLOSS license such as MIT or Apache-2.0; PROJECT.md does not pick between them (owner must choose).

records.title: Name: adjudicate, CLI command adj
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. The tool is named adjudicate; the CLI command is `adj`; the Go module path is github.com/squalor-xyz/adjudicate. Replaces the working name 'dlog' (assumption C14, retired).

records.title: Runtime: Go, standard library only
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. Go (installed: go1.27.2 via Homebrew), standard library only, for runtime and tests (the `testing` package). Not Python. Any new dependency needs owner approval. Replaces assumption C15 (retired).

records.title: Record format: Markdown body with JSON frontmatter
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. One file per record: a Markdown body with JSON frontmatter, read and written with encoding/json. No TOML and no hand-written TOML parser or emitter. Owner's reason: the Go standard library has no TOML. The frontmatter delimiter is an implementer decision under the standing rule (C32). Replaces assumption C16 (retired).

records.title: IDs: sequential, lint collision detection, renumber command
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). Sequential IDs: the next free ID comes from scanning the store; lint detects collisions; a renumber command resolves them. Which record keeps a colliding ID and the renumber command's name are implementer decisions under the standing rule (C32). Replaces assumption C17 (retired).

records.title: Owner-only decide: convention in v1
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). Convention plus an AGENTS.md rule in v1: only the owner makes the decide transition. decided_by is recorded on each decision (attribution, not authentication); lint warns when it is missing. No git hook or signed commits in v1. Replaces assumption C18 (retired).

records.title: Scope: per-repo in v1
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). v1 works on one repo's store; a cross-repo inbox is Later-tier work. Replaces assumption C19 (retired).

records.title: Store: decisions/ at repo root, configurable
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (recommendation accepted). The store defaults to decisions/ at the repo root, and the config can change the path. Replaces assumption C20 (retired).

records.title: Record kind: status alone, no kind field
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. Records have no kind field; status alone carries it: open = a question; decided, rejected, withdrawn and superseded = answered. Replaces assumption C21 (retired).

records.title: License: GPL-3.0-or-later
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. The project is licensed GPL-3.0-or-later. Replaces assumption C22 (retired).

records.title: Standing rule: implementer decides unfixed interface details
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15. Interface details not fixed by PROJECT.md or the owner's decisions are decided by the slice implementer: for example the config file name and format, how options and tradeoffs are passed on the CLI, how decided_by is supplied, check's match rule and exit codes, the context fields, whether lint warnings change the exit code, which record keeps a colliding ID, and the renumber command's name. The implementer records each such choice in the slicer catalog as a decision with a one-line reason; the reviewer checks it. The owner may overrule later.

records.title: Go caches and checks stay inside the repo
records.body: Owner constraint 2026-10-15. GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE and GOPATH point at a gitignored .cache/ under the repo root. No make: the env vars are documented in AGENTS.md and set by a small scripts/env.sh or an equivalent that the scaffolding slice (S02) decides. Tests run with go test ./... and go vet ./..., plus a gofmt check (gofmt -l lists no files).

records.title: Exit codes: 0 success, 1 failed operation or check, 2 usage error
records.body: Matches slicer's exit codes (1 failed check, 2 usage or validation error), so agents read both tools the same way.

records.title: CLI layout: cmd/adj calls internal/cli.Run with injected I/O
records.body: Run takes args, stdin, stdout and stderr and returns the exit code, so tests run the CLI in-process with buffers and main stays one line.

records.title: Help flags: --help and -h print usage to stdout with exit 0; usage errors go to stderr with exit 2
records.body: Help is requested output on stdout; a missing or unknown command is an error, so its usage goes to stderr.

records.title: env.sh extras: GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, GOFLAGS=-modcacherw, GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR under .cache/tmp
records.body: The workspace sandbox keeps Go inside the repo: no toolchain or module downloads, temp files under .cache/tmp, and -modcacherw lets the in-repo module cache be deleted without chmod.

records.title: .gitignore: drop build/ and dist/, drop Python entries, add /adj, /bin/, *.test, *.out
records.body: No Python and no build/ or dist/ output: Check builds to .cache/bin/adj and a bare go build writes /adj, so both are ignored.

records.title: LICENSE is a stub until the owner supplies the full GPL-3.0 text and copyright holder
records.body: No GPL-3.0 text exists in the adjudicate repo and the workspace has no network, so the stub carries the SPDX line, the or-later notice and TODO(owner) markers.
records.reason: Replaced by the full GPL-3.0 text and NOTICE (owner supplied the text and named Squalor LLC, 2026-10-15).

records.title: env.sh: source from bash or zsh only; refuses to run unless the derived root has go.mod
records.body: Dash and other shells that are not bash or zsh cannot report the sourced path, and a wrong root would send caches and temp files outside the repo, so the script checks go.mod before it exports or creates anything.

records.title: Record field types: dates as YYYY-MM-DD strings, integer ids, supersedes a list, superseded_by one id
records.body: A string in time.DateOnly form encodes as itself with encoding/json and keeps files deterministic. An old record is superseded by exactly one record, while a new record may replace several, so supersedes is []int and superseded_by is int (0 omitted).

records.title: Required fields: id>0, title, status, created always; rationale and decided_at once answered; decision once decided or superseded; superseded_by once superseded
records.body: Rejected and withdrawn records need a why (PROJECT.md reject/withdraw --why) and a date but no decision text. decided_by is never required because lint warns instead (C27).

records.title: History entry shape: {date, event, note}; event is the transition verb (ask, decide, reject, withdraw, supersede)
records.body: A flat list of three small fields stays readable in JSON frontmatter. Supersede puts 'by N' in note; creation (ask) is written by the code that creates the record, since model transitions start from open.

records.title: Recommendation shape: {label, reasoning}, label must be one of the options
records.body: The table says the option label plus reasoning; two named fields keep the label machine-checkable and the reasoning free text.

records.title: Transition API: Decide, Reject, Withdraw and Supersede mutate the record in place, take the date as a YYYY-MM-DD string, and leave the record untouched on error
records.body: Each builds and validates a copy before storing it, so a failed transition changes nothing, appends no history and never writes into the caller's slice. Errors match ErrInvalid; a status mismatch also matches ErrInvalidTransition.

records.title: Supersede changes only the old record; setting the new record's supersedes link is the caller's job
records.body: The slice scopes a transition to one record and one history entry; linking the pair across two files belongs to the supersede command and store.

records.title: Validate checks each history entry: a YYYY-MM-DD date and one of the five known events; blank decision and rationale text count as missing
records.body: A hand-edited file with a bad history date, an unknown event or whitespace-only why would otherwise load as valid; title already rejected blank text.

records.title: Record fence: --- lines around the JSON frontmatter
records.body: The file opens with a --- line and the frontmatter ends at the first later line that is exactly ---; encoding/json writes no raw newline inside a string, so a fence cannot occur in the JSON, and body lines such as --- or } pass through intact. LF only: a file that starts with a byte order mark is rejected (file starts with a byte order mark), and so is a file whose frontmatter lines end in CR (CRLF line endings are not supported); both name the reason and match ErrInvalid. A closing fence at end of file with no newline is accepted, with an empty body.

records.title: Markdown body is Record.Body with json:"-", kept verbatim
records.body: Each structured field lives once in the frontmatter and no field is repeated into the body, so the body is free Markdown that cannot drift from the fields.

records.title: Marshal and Unmarshal both validate
records.body: Marshal refuses a record that Validate rejects and Unmarshal never returns an invalid record, so the strict read path cannot load a file the writer would not produce.

records.title: Parse is the exported lenient decode with no Validate
records.body: Lint (S14) lives outside this package and must report invalid records rather than fail to load them; Unmarshal is Parse plus Validate.

records.title: A non-empty body gets one final newline when it lacks one
records.body: Every file ends with a newline, so output is POSIX text and stable; a body that already ends in a newline is written byte for byte.

records.title: Malformed and invalid files match ErrInvalid
records.body: Callers branch on one sentinel for every bad file, and the message still names the file.

records.title: WriteFile uses os.WriteFile, not temp file and rename
records.body: Records are small text files; an atomic replace is left to the store slice if it needs one.

records.title: ReadFile and WriteFile live in model/file.go, so model gains I/O
records.body: The slice Files list places them in model; they are the package's only file I/O, so AGENTS.md:23 and the record.go package doc change with them.

records.title: Config: .adjudicate.json at the repo root, one JSON object with an optional store key
records.body: Unknown keys, an absolute store and a store that leaves the root are errors (invalid config); a missing file means the defaults (store decisions/). One standard-library format, and a typo in a key does not pass silently. The store-path check is lexical: a symlinked store can still point outside the root, and the config is owner-authored.

records.title: Root discovery: nearest directory, from the working directory up, holding .adjudicate.json as a regular file
records.body: store.FindRoot returns it, or ErrNoRoot if none; adj init (later) writes the file. The config file is the one marker the owner already configures, and a directory of that name does not count. The walk goes to the file system root with no git boundary, so an .adjudicate.json in an ancestor directory applies.

records.title: Record file name: <ID padded to four digits>-<slug>.md; slug is the title's lowercase ASCII letters and digits joined by -, at most 60 bytes, untitled if empty
records.body: Non-ASCII characters and punctuation act as separators, so names are portable and diff-stable; 60 bytes keeps paths short; IDs above 9999 keep all digits.

records.title: Record files are found by name: regular file, four or more digits above zero, then -, text and .md; the ID comes from the name
records.body: A file that does not parse still reserves its ID, so a broken file never lets Create reuse a number; List and Get reject a file whose record ID differs from its name.

records.title: Duplicate IDs: List returns every file in ID then file-name order; Get and Update fail with ErrDuplicateID
records.body: Detecting and renumbering collisions is S15; the store must not silently pick one file, and Create still allocates one past the highest ID.

records.title: List is strict: the first unreadable or invalid record file is an error naming it
records.body: Every command needs records that satisfy the model; lint (S14) uses model.Parse itself to report invalid files instead of loading them.

records.title: Store writes go through a synced temp file: Update renames it over the record, Create links it into place and never replaces a file
records.body: Answers C54 for the store. The record is written to a .adj-*.tmp file (names start with a dot, so never taken for records) and fsynced. Update renames it over the record; after a crash the file is the old record or the new one, but the directory is not fsynced, so which one is not guaranteed. Create links it into place, so it can never overwrite a file; the link also keeps a reader from seeing half a record. Accepted limit: os.Link fails on file systems without hard links and there is no fallback. Concurrent creates in one checkout are serialised by the ID lock (C114, S23), which covers the scan and the link; collisions between branches or clones are not, and stay with lint (S14) and renumber (S15) (C26). Before S23 the scan was not locked, so two creates with different titles could both get the same ID.

records.title: Create ignores the ID in the record and adds no history entry; the store directory is made on first Create; a missing directory is an empty store; Update keeps the file path
records.body: The ID is the store's to allocate (C26); the ask command writes the history entry and date (C43); an unrenamed file keeps git history and links to it.

records.title: Permissions and retry: new records are 0644, Update keeps the old file's permission bits, and Create retries up to three times when its file name is taken
records.body: os.CreateTemp makes 0600 files, so the store sets the mode itself: 0644 for a new record (git-friendly, umask-independent) and the replaced file's bits on Update so a chosen mode survives. When the link finds the name taken (a writer that does not take the ID lock, a directory, or a platform with no lock), Create rescans and takes the next ID, then gives up with an error wrapping os.ErrExist that names the target file. The retry stays as a second line of defence behind the ID lock (C114, S23); before S23 there was no locking, which was the owner's design call.

records.title: Root selection: --root DIR on every command, plus cli.Env.Root and Env.Stop; explicit roots are never searched
records.body: Tests run in temp dirs under the repo's own .cache, where walking up from the cwd could find the repo's real .adjudicate.json. --root DIR (flag wins) or the injected Env.Root names the root as it is: init uses it as is, other commands need DIR/.adjudicate.json in it. With neither, init uses the working directory and other commands search upward from it with store.FindRoot; Env.Stop bounds that walk (store.FindRootWithin, formerly the unexported findRoot) so a discovery test cannot leave its temp dir. --root is per command, not global, so it can sit among the other flags.

records.title: Run keeps its signature; RunWith(Env, ...) takes clock, environment, working directory and root
records.body: C35 fixed Run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) for main; tests need a fixed clock, a fake environment and no use of the real cwd, so Run calls RunWith with the zero Env (real time.Now, os.Getenv, os.Getwd).

records.title: Flags: one FlagSet per command; flags may follow positionals; -h/--help print the command usage to stdout (exit 0)
records.body: parseInterspersed splits arguments itself (a flag value is taken as the value even if it looks like a flag or is --) and then calls FlagSet.Parse once; a lone - and anything after -- are positional. Errors and usage go to stderr with exit 2, matching C36.

records.title: adj ask --option LABEL:SUMMARY, tradeoffs as --tradeoffs LABEL:TEXT; both split at the first colon
records.body: A separate flag keeps the PROJECT.md --option shape and keeps colons in summaries unambiguous (a third colon field in --option would not). The label must name an option and each option takes one --tradeoffs; labels and texts are trimmed; blank labels are refused.

records.title: adj ask recommendation reasoning: --reasoning TEXT, only with --recommend
records.body: The recommendation record has label and reasoning (C44); a flag next to --recommend is the smallest way to fill the second field, and reasoning with no recommendation is a usage error rather than silently dropped.

records.title: asked_by: --by NAME, else the ADJ_ASKED_BY environment variable, else left blank
records.body: Agents set one environment variable once instead of repeating a flag; a blank is better than a guessed identity (C27 treats attribution as a convention). The flag wins so one command can override.

records.title: adj ask context: --context TEXT, or --stdin to read it; both is a usage error; trailing newlines of stdin are trimmed
records.body: Long context is easier to pipe than to quote. Trimming only CR and LF at the end keeps leading indentation and inner blank lines, and the context field carries no stray final newline.

records.title: adj init writes {"store": "decisions"} and creates the store directory; it acts on DIR or the cwd only, keeps an existing valid config, and prints initialized or already initialized
records.body: Spelling the one setting out shows the owner what to change (C56, C29). init never searches upward, so running it in a subdirectory starts a new root on purpose; a second run changes nothing, and an invalid or non-regular config fails with exit 1 before anything is created.

records.title: Exit codes for init and ask: bad arguments exit 2 before any store access; no config (run adj init), an invalid config or a failed write exit 1
records.body: Follows C34: bad input is a usage error whatever the state of the store, and a missing store is a failed operation. ErrNoRoot is mapped to a message that says to run adj init.

records.title: adj ask prints the new ID as a plain integer on stdout; created is the clock's local date
records.body: One machine-readable line (1, not 0001) is easy for agents to feed to later commands; the date is time.DateOnly of the injected clock, as C41 stores dates.

records.title: adj ask tags: trimmed, blank is a usage error, repeats are dropped (first one kept, order kept)
records.body: An agent that repeats a tag meant the same tag, so de-duplicating is kinder than an exit 2; a blank tag is a typo and stays an error. --recommend is trimmed like option labels (C68).

records.title: adj init removes the config it just wrote if creating the store directory fails; an existing config is never removed
records.body: A failed init must not leave a half-initialised repo, or ask would pass the config check and then fail; a config the owner wrote is theirs and stays.

records.title: decided_by: --by NAME, else ADJ_DECIDED_BY, else blank
records.body: Reuses the C70 asked_by pattern for decide, reject and withdraw, so an agent sets one variable once; attribution only, not authentication (C27).

records.title: decide takes an OPTION or --text, never both; OPTION is trimmed
records.body: Exactly one answer, as S07 states; the positional OPTION is trimmed like ask labels (C68), so " a " names option a.

records.title: An OPTION the record does not offer is a usage error (exit 2)
records.body: Option labels live in the record, so this check runs after the record is read; unknown ID, not open and store failures stay exit 1 (C34).

records.title: --why and --text are stored as typed; blank is a usage error
records.body: Matches --reasoning and --context (C69, C71), which keep their text; a blank reason or answer is refused before the store is read, as blank tags are (C75).

records.title: decide, reject and withdraw print the record ID; the ID must be a positive integer
records.body: Same one-line output as adj ask (C74) so agents can chain commands; a non-number or 0 is a usage error (exit 2).

records.title: Handlers: one file per command; UsageError moves to commands/errors.go
records.body: S06 review note: cli.go held every handler. init.go, ask.go and decide.go hold the handlers (decide.go has decide, reject and withdraw, which share flags and the store path); init and ask moved as is. Deviation from the Files list (cli.go, decide_test.go).

records.title: An explicit empty --recommend is a usage error, as --tag "" is
records.body: S06 review note: --recommend "" was treated as absent; fsSet makes it exit 2 like a blank tag (C75).

records.title: A record that is not open is refused before OPTION is checked
records.body: Refines C79 (S07 review): a decided record given an unknown OPTION exits 1 with the status error, because the status is the first thing the transition checks. Exit 2 is left for an OPTION the open record does not offer.

records.title: A change to a record that is not open names its status and the change
records.body: Message: record N is S; only an open record can be V (V = decided, rejected or withdrawn), in place of the model text invalid record: transition not allowed. A notOpenError keeps the model error reachable through Unwrap, so errors.Is(err, model.ErrInvalidTransition) still holds.

records.title: S08 list --json: one object with a records array
records.body: An object with a named key lets later fields such as counts be added without breaking readers, which a bare array would not; an empty store gives {"records": []}.

records.title: S08 show --json: the record object, same shape as each list entry
records.body: One record shape for both commands so an agent parses one format; keys are the record file JSON names and empty keys are omitted, as in the file.

records.title: S08 show prints the body and emits it as body
records.body: The body is the owner free Markdown, kept out of the frontmatter (C49) but still their text, so show prints it and JSON gives a body key only when it is non-empty.

records.title: S08 list --tag repeats and every given tag must match
records.body: Mirrors the repeatable --tag of ask; a repeat narrows the result, consistent with the AND rule for combined filters.

records.title: S08 list filters combine with AND
records.body: Each filter given must match, so every added flag narrows the result and no filter lists every record (slice proposal).

records.title: S08 filter values: known status, no blank tag or key
records.body: Bad values exit 2 before the store is read (C73); a blank value is a typo, not no filter (C75, C83); --key matches the stored key as typed, since ask stores it untrimmed.

records.title: S08 list order and empty results
records.body: List keeps store.List order (ID, then file name per C60); no match prints nothing in text and an empty records array in JSON with exit 0, because an empty answer is not a failure.

records.title: S08 text layout for list and show
records.body: List prints one aligned line per record (ID, status, title) for grep; show prints a labelled line per set field so one field is easy to find, with multi-line values indented under their label.

records.title: S08 show and list arguments
records.body: show takes one positive ID, and a bad ID is exit 2 as in decide (C81); list takes no positional arguments, since a stray word is a typo to report, not to ignore; an unknown or duplicate ID is exit 1 (C34).

records.title: S08 handlers in cli/show.go and cli/list.go
records.body: C82 wants one handler file per command; the slice Files list omitted these two, so they are added and named in AGENTS.md Layout.

records.title: S08 ask rejects a blank --key (exit 2)
records.body: ask stored a whitespace-only --key that list --key can never match (C91); like --tag it is now a usage error, while a real key is still stored as typed.

records.title: S09 inbox arguments: adj inbox [--json] [--root DIR], no filters or positional arguments
records.body: The slice asks for open questions only; a stray word or a list filter is a usage error (exit 2) rather than silently ignored (C94), and adj list --status/--tag/--key already filter records.

records.title: S09 inbox order: created date, then ID, ascending
records.body: Oldest question first answers the slice; created is a YYYY-MM-DD string so text order is date order (C41), and ID breaks ties and matches the store order. A sorted copy is made in commands, since store.List order is ID order (C92). The sort is stable, so equal records (same ID and date, C60) keep store.List order.

records.title: S09 inbox --json: the list shape, {"records": [...]} of full record objects
records.body: Reuses render.RecordsJSON (C86, C87) so an agent parses one record shape; options with tradeoffs and the recommendation are already keys of the record. An empty inbox gives {"records": []}.

records.title: S09 inbox text layout: 'ID  title' then indented Created, Context, Options, Recommendation and Reasoning
records.body: The header keeps the ID and title greppable like list lines (C93); the owner needs when it was asked (the sort key), the options with summary and tradeoffs, and the asker's recommendation to answer in one batch. Context is shown too: owner decision 2026-10-15 (review of S09), multi-line context indented like other fields and omitted when empty. Key, tags and history are left to adj show.

records.title: S09 empty inbox prints nothing in text and an empty array in JSON, exit 0
records.body: Same as an empty list (C92): an empty answer is not a failure, and a script can test for no output.

records.title: S09 render trims trailing line breaks of option summaries, tradeoffs and history notes
records.body: S08 gate note: cont() indented the empty line after a trailing newline, printing a spaces-only line; these values now go through the same trim as other fields, and a value that is only line breaks counts as unset. writeField and writeOptions are shared by show and inbox.

records.title: S09 handler files: cli/inbox.go, commands/inbox.go, render/inbox.go, plus commands/inbox_test.go and render/inbox_test.go
records.body: C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list names only cli/inbox_test.go; the oldest-first tie-break is only testable on unsorted input in package commands, and the text layout is tested in render beside the other golden tests.

records.title: S09 docs/json.md inbox example is checked by a test
records.body: TestInboxJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample runs the CLI on a seeded repo and compares its output to the first json block of the inbox section, so the documented shape cannot drift from the real output.

records.title: S10 check match rule: the trimmed query as a case-insensitive substring of title, key, any tag or the decision text
records.body: The slice proposal. The rationale is not searched: the slice names titles, keys, tags and decision text, and a rationale hit would report a record that is about something else. A blank query matches nothing (query.Search) and is a usage error in the CLI (C109).

records.title: S10 check reports every status: decided and open as such, rejected, withdrawn and superseded in a closed list
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (S10 review), replacing the first rule that hid closed records. Search covers all statuses. A rejected, withdrawn or superseded match goes in the closed list, shown with its status (and superseded_by), so an agent sees that a topic was already closed and does not re-ask it. Closed records never count as decided.

records.title: S10 check result precedence: decided, then open, then closed, then not found; both lists are always reported
records.body: Result is decided if the decided list is not empty (including the decided end of a supersede chain, C113), else open, else closed (a new result word), else not found. The decided record is what an agent must follow, so it wins; the other lists are still reported so an agent sees the follow-up question or the closed history. Exit codes do not depend on the result (C108).

records.title: S10 check exit codes: 0 for every completed check (decided, open, closed and not found), 1 a failed check, 2 a usage error
records.body: The slice proposal, kept for agent scripts and confirmed by the owner in the S10 review: a non-zero exit means the check could not run (no repo, bad config, an unreadable record file), so a broken store is never mistaken for not found and then asked about. The answer is in the first line of the text or the result key of the JSON; C34's 1 and 2 are unchanged. Documented in the check usage, docs/json.md and AGENTS.md.

records.title: S10 check arguments: exactly one QUERY; none, several or a blank one is a usage error (exit 2) before the store is read
records.body: A stray word is a typo to report (C94), and several words would need a rule for joining them, so the user quotes a query with spaces; the message says so. A blank query would match everything or nothing, so it is refused like a blank tag (C75, C91).

records.title: S10 check output: first line is the result word; JSON is {query, result, decided, open, closed} with list-shaped records
records.body: Text: decided, open, closed or not found on line one, then ID  status  title per record (decided, open, closed), with a decided record's Decision and Rationale indented under it, and a closed record's Superseded by (superseded only) then Rationale (C132). JSON: query (trimmed), result, and the decided, open and closed record arrays, always present and never null, so an agent reads one record shape (C86, C87). The result word is spelled the same in both: not found.

records.title: S10 handler and render files: cli/check.go, commands/check.go, render/check.go, plus commands/check_test.go and render/check_test.go
records.body: C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list names only query/search.go, commands/check.go and cli/check_test.go; the text and JSON output is tested in render beside the other golden tests, and the blank-query rule in commands. render/json.go gained jsonRecords, shared with RecordsJSON.

records.title: S10 docs/json.md check example is checked by a test
records.body: TestCheckJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample runs the CLI on a seeded repo and compares its output to the first json block of the check section, as C104 does for inbox, so the documented shape cannot drift from the real output.

records.title: S10 check follows superseded_by from a superseded match to a decided record
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15 (S10 review). A superseded match stays in closed; its superseded_by is followed through superseded records, bounded by visiting each record once, to the end of the chain. If the end is a decided record it is added to decided (once, in ID order, even if it also matched). A chain that stops at a missing ID, at a record that is neither superseded nor decided, or in a repeat (a loop) adds nothing. This way an agent that finds a replaced decision is led to the decision in force.

records.title: ID allocation is locked with flock
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15: store.Create holds an advisory flock (unix) across the ID scan and the link, so concurrent asks in one checkout cannot share an ID. Branch/clone collisions stay with lint/renumber (S14/S15). Implemented in S23, after S15.

records.title: S11 context selects status decided only, in ID order
records.body: The slice says only decided appears; superseded records are left out because their replacement is decided (C113 leads check the same way). Order is store.List order (ID, C92), so the same store gives the same bytes.

records.title: S11 context entry fields: id, title, key, decision, first line of the rationale
records.body: The slice proposal: enough to follow a decision (what and why in one line) without options, context, tags or history; adj show has the rest. key is left out when unset, as in a record (C87).

records.title: S11 context rationale is the first non-blank line, trimmed
records.body: A rationale is free text that may run to paragraphs; the first line keeps entries compact (Risks: context bloat). Leading blank lines are skipped so a rationale that starts with a line break still shows a reason. The decision text is kept whole, since it is the answer.

records.title: S11 context --format md|json, default md, exact lowercase; any other value is a usage error
records.body: The slice proposal; md is the form an agent reads or pastes. Checked before the store is read (C73), like a bad status (C91); an explicit empty value is refused too (C83), not read as the default.

records.title: S11 context md layout: a list entry '- ID title [key]: decision' then '  Rationale: first line'; no header; empty prints nothing
records.body: Compact and diff-stable: one list line per decision with the key in brackets (omitted when unset), the rationale indented under it, a multi-line decision continuing on lines indented four spaces. No header, so an empty result is no output (C101) and the caller adds its own framing. Reuses writeField and cont from text.go.

records.title: S11 context --format json: {"decisions": [{id, title, key?, decision, rationale?}]}, empty is an empty array
records.body: An object with a named key lets fields be added later (C86); the key is decisions, not records, because an entry is not the full record object. docs/json.md has the shape and TestContextJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample checks the example against real output (C104).

records.title: S11 context --tag repeats, every tag must match, trimmed; --key-prefix is a plain string prefix of the stored key as typed; blank values are usage errors
records.body: Reuses list's rules (C89, C91): AND semantics, trimmed tags, key matched as typed. The prefix is not dot-aware (storage also matches storagex) because the slice names a key prefix and a plain prefix is the least surprising; a record with no key never matches. query.Filter gains KeyPrefix.

records.title: S11 context takes no positional arguments; flags may come before or after; --json is not a context flag
records.body: A stray word is a typo to report (C94, C97). The format flag is --format as the slice names it, so list's --json does not carry over.

records.title: S11 handler files: cli/context.go, commands/context.go, render/context.go, plus query/filter_test.go and render/testdata/context.md, context.json
records.body: C82 wants one handler file per command. The slice Files list omits query (Filter.KeyPrefix and its test). The golden files in render/testdata are shared: render tests build the four records by hand and cli tests read the same files through a seeded store.

records.title: S12 adj ai prints the embedded snippet internal/commands/ai.md and takes no flag or argument, not even --root
records.body: It reads no repo, so --root would do nothing; a stray argument is a typo to report, as for inbox and context (C94, C97, C122). Markdown file via embed so the snippet reads as it will be pasted.

records.title: S12 the snippet is tested against the CLI: every adj command it names has --help, every flag in an adj code span is a whole word in that command's usage, every ADJ_ variable is in a usage, at most 1800 bytes
records.body: The snippet is pasted into other repos' AGENTS.md and cannot be checked there, so a rename or removed flag must fail here; the size cap keeps it token-cheap (Risks: adoption). Whole-word matching so --reason does not pass for --reasoning.

records.title: S12 the snippet tells agents to check, read (context, show), ask and withdraw their own question, and never to run adj decide or adj reject
records.body: Owner confirmed 2026-10-15: agents may withdraw their own questions (never another agent's or the owner's; C130). C27 makes only the decide transition the owner's; withdraw is the asker's own close and records no decision, so an agent can drop a stale question. adj supersede is not named until S13 adds it.

records.title: S12 json shape test: docs/json.md first json block under each command heading is the shape; show and list are pinned by a fixture that matches their examples byte for byte; record keys must be in the Keys of a record table, which must equal model.Record json tags plus body
records.body: Record keys are omitted when empty (C87), so a key list taken from output would vary; a byte-exact fixture pins show and list, the table is pinned to the model by reflection, and context entries are checked against their own table. docsJSONExample and jsonBlockUnder moved to jsonshape_test.go so one convention reads the docs (S09 review, C104).

records.title: S12 withdraw usage describes --by as who withdrew it; docs/json.md context rationale row says the first non-blank line
records.body: S07 gate nit: who decided reads oddly for a withdrawal (reject keeps who decided); S11 gate nit: code, C117 and AGENTS.md already say first non-blank line, the docs table said first line.

records.title: S12 snippet flag drift check: a flag in any code span is checked against the nearest preceding adj CMD span
records.body: Review LOW: prose spans such as 'or pass --by NAME' were not covered; attributing by position keeps the prose natural without moving every flag into an adj span.

records.title: S12 snippet limits: withdraw only your own question and with --by NAME (ADJ_DECIDED_BY is the owner's and not named); on closed read adj show ID and never re-ask a rejected question; on no repo tell the owner, do not run adj init
records.body: Review MEDIUM/LOW: withdraw records decided_by, so an agent names itself with --by; a rejected question was decided against, so re-asking it wastes the owner's batch; init is the owner's setup step. Refines C126.

records.title: LICENSE is the full GPL-3.0 text; NOTICE holds the Squalor LLC copyright
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15: copyright holder is Squalor LLC. LICENSE is the verbatim GPL-3.0 text supplied by the owner (the license forbids changing it), so the copyright line and the or-later notice live in NOTICE.

records.title: check text shows the rationale under closed records
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-15: adj check text prints the rationale under rejected, withdrawn and superseded matches, so an agent sees why a topic was closed. Implemented in S24.

records.title: S13 adj supersede OLD --by NEW [--root DIR]: --by is the replacing record's ID, there is no --why and no who flag
records.body: The slice names OLD --by NEW. --by here is an ID, not an author as in decide, so the owner's name is not recorded: model.Supersede takes no rationale or actor and the old record keeps its own rationale. Extra arguments, a missing --by, and a --by that is not a positive integer are usage errors (exit 2).

records.title: S13 supersede prints OLD's ID and exits 0; OLD equal to NEW is a usage error (2); unknown ID or a record that is not decided is exit 1, OLD checked first
records.body: Like decide, reject and withdraw it prints the ID of the record it changed (C74). Equal IDs are bad input that needs no record, so they exit 2 before the store is looked for (C73); a missing or not-decided record is a failed operation (C34), and the message names the status, as decide's does.

records.title: S13 model.LinkSupersedes(r, old, date) is the new record's half of a supersede: adds old to supersedes once, appends one supersede history entry with note 'supersedes N'
records.body: C46 leaves the new record's link to the caller; apply is unexported, so a model function keeps the same validate-a-copy, record-untouched-on-error guarantee (C45) instead of duplicating it in the command. The history event is supersede, the five events of C43 stay unchanged, and the note mirrors 'by N' on the old record. The slice allows extending transition.go only if needed; this is why.

records.title: S13 supersede validates both records in memory, writes OLD first, and if NEW then fails puts OLD back; if that fails too the error says the store is inconsistent
records.body: Two files cannot be written atomically (C62 is per file). OLD first because the worst leftover, OLD superseded and NEW decided without its link back, still leaves one decision in force (check and context agree); NEW first could leave two decided records that contradict each other. The restore makes the common failure leave both records unchanged; the error names the leftover state when it cannot.

records.title: S13 the agent snippet's never-run list gains adj supersede
records.body: Superseding changes a decision, so it is owner-only like decide and reject (C27, C126). The S12 gate note asked for it; ai_test checks the list names it, as the drift test only checks that named commands exist.

records.title: S24 check text closed records: full rationale, after Superseded by
records.body: Closed records print the whole rationale through writeField (multi-line under the label, trailing breaks trimmed, empty omitted), not the first line as adj context does (C117): context is a compact export of settled answers, while a closed record's reason is the thing check exists to show, and the slice requires the C102 continuation. The label is Rationale, as for decided records. A superseded record prints Superseded by first, then Rationale: the pointer to the decision in force leads, the old reason follows. Implements C132.

records.title: S14 lint lives in internal/lint, with handler files cli/lint.go, commands/lint.go, render/lint.go; store gains Files()
records.body: The slice allows internal/lint or internal/query; lint reads files and checks records across a store, which query (pure functions over records) does not. Files() returns (ID, name, path) from the C59 name rule so lint does not copy it (S05 note); C82 wants one handler file per command, and render/lint.go holds the text and JSON output.

records.title: S14 lint exit codes: 1 if any finding is an error or lint could not run, 0 otherwise (warnings alone exit 0); findings go to stdout
records.body: The slice proposal: a missing decided_by is advice (C27), so CI that runs lint is not failed by it. Exit 1 covers a failed check as in C34; a run that could not start (no repo, unreadable store directory) also exits 1 with stderr only, so a script reads stdout for the findings. Usage errors exit 2.

records.title: S14 lint text output: one line per finding 'FILE: record ID: SEVERITY: CHECK: MESSAGE', then 'N errors, M warnings'; a clean store prints nothing
records.body: Compiler-style lines are greppable and clickable in CI logs, the count line tells a human how bad it is, and an empty answer prints nothing as for an empty list or inbox (C92, C101). Findings are sorted by record ID, then check, then file; File is relative to the repo root with slashes.

records.title: S14 lint --json: {errors, warnings, findings: [{id, file, severity, check, message}]}, findings always an array
records.body: An object with named keys leaves room for more fields (C86); the counts save a reader from counting, and a clean store is an empty array, not null. docs/json.md has the shape and TestLintJSONMatchesTheDocumentedExample checks its example against real output (C104); lint is added to the top-level key test.

records.title: S14 lint checks: parse, fields, id-mismatch, dangling-link, supersede-state, supersede-cycle, key-conflict (errors) and decided-by (warning)
records.body: Defect classes of C08 plus the S03 note and the S14 review: fields is one finding per model.Validate rule, and also a link to the file's own ID when the record's id differs (Validate compares with the id); id-mismatch flags a record whose id is not the ID in its file name, which store.List refuses (not raised when the id is missing or not positive: fields says that); supersede-state flags superseded_by on a non-superseded record (Validate lets it through); a cycle is a strongly connected set in a directed graph built from both link fields: superseded_by gives an edge old to new, and each supersedes entry X on a record gives an edge X to that record (so 'both directions' means both fields, not an undirected graph); one finding per member, naming only records that have a file (dangling-link reports a missing ID); key-conflict covers decided records only, key trimmed, case-sensitive (superseded, open, rejected and withdrawn do not conflict). decided-by warns for status decided only (C27); reject and withdraw record who acted, not a decision. id-mismatch is its own check so a script can tell it from a missing field.

records.title: S14 lint identifies a record by the ID in its file name, and a link dangles only if no file has that ID
records.body: C59: a file that does not parse still holds its ID, so a link to a broken file is not dangling and a parse finding carries the ID. A record whose id differs from its file name is an id-mismatch error (S14 review). Not done, left for S15 or the owner: two files with one ID, and a raw check for case-variant or duplicate JSON keys (S04 note).

records.title: S14 the agent snippet does not name adj lint
records.body: Lint is an owner and CI check of the record files; agents write records only through adj, so they have no use for it, and the snippet stays under 1800 bytes (C125). lint takes no argument and only --json and --root.

records.title: S15 renumber keeper: the record created first keeps a colliding ID, the file name breaks a tie; every other record gets the next free ID
records.body: The slice proposal. created is a YYYY-MM-DD string, so text order is date order (C41); the file name makes the result deterministic. Of the files sharing an ID, the others are taken in the same order and given one past the highest ID in the store, colliding IDs in ascending order, and keep their name text (0003-foo.md becomes 0008-foo.md) so the slug is not re-derived from a title that may have changed. Implemented in store.Renumber.

records.title: S15 renumber links: never rewritten; if any record links to a colliding ID renumber lists the links and exits 1 with nothing changed, unless --keep-links, which leaves them on the record that keeps the ID and lists them on stderr
records.body: A link to an ID that two files share was written for one of them and nothing in the files says which, so any rewrite is a guess; leaving them silently would change what they mean (lint would be clean afterwards). Refusing first makes the owner look, and --keep-links is the explicit acceptance; a link that meant the moved record is a one-line edit by hand. Links are found in every record file, the colliding ones included, and a link listed twice counts once.

records.title: S15 renumber writes the new file before removing the old one, and undoes a move whose old file cannot be removed
records.body: A crash between the two steps leaves both files, where rename-then-rewrite would leave a file whose id differs from its name. The new file is a synced temp file linked into place, so it never replaces anything (C62); the store directory is synced before the old file goes (C157). If the old file cannot be removed the new one is removed again; if that fails too the error names both files and says to delete the new one. Moves completed earlier stay and are printed. After a crash the old file is a stale copy: renumber refuses to run until the owner deletes it, and lint reports it as renumber-leftover (C156).

records.title: S15 renumber leaves history notes as written; the move adds one history entry with event renumber and note 'from N'
records.body: Answers the S13 note: 'by N' and 'supersedes N' record what happened at the time, and since renumber rewrites no link, rewriting the notes that name the same IDs would make them disagree with the links. The new event renumber (model.EventRenumber, model.Renumber, validated on a copy as in C45) is the only way to append a history entry, because the five events of C43 do not fit; this touches internal/model, which the slice Files list does not name, and docs/json.md lists the event.

records.title: S15 command is adj renumber [--keep-links] [--root DIR], not lint --fix; it prints one line per move and has no --json
records.body: lint is read-only (TestLintChangesNothing) and its exit code means findings, so a fix flag would blur both. The command takes no argument, prints 'OLD-FILE -> NEW-FILE (id N -> M)' per move and nothing when there is no collision (exit 0, as an empty lint or list prints nothing, C92, C141), exit 1 when it stops or fails, 2 for a usage error. No --json: the moves are for the owner to read, so there is no JSON shape to document.

records.title: S15 renumber reads every record file when there is a collision and checks every move before writing; with no collision it reads nothing
records.body: Any file may hold a link to a colliding ID, so an unreadable or unparseable file stops the run, naming it (lint tells the owner what is wrong). A moved record must stay valid under its new ID; checking all moves in memory first means a refusal changes nothing. With no shared ID, Renumber only scans file names, so a broken file elsewhere is no obstacle and the store is untouched.

records.title: S15 lint duplicate-id: an error on every file that shares the ID, the message lists all of them; a link to such an ID is not dangling; a link listed twice is reported once
records.body: The slice asks that lint name both files. One finding per file (like supersede-cycle) puts the finding on each file in the editor and CI log; the message names them all. dangling-link still means no file has the ID (C144). The repeated-link dedupe is the S14 gate note: [7,7] gave two identical findings. The raw JSON key case and duplicate check (S04 note) is still not done.

records.title: S15 the agent snippet tells agents to report a duplicate ID to the owner and not run adj renumber
records.body: Renumber rewrites and renames record files and changes which record an ID names, so it is the owner's, like decide and supersede (C27, C137). The agent may hit the collision as 'more than one record has this id' from show or check; the snippet says to tell the owner, in one added sentence (still under 1800 bytes, C125). adj lint stays unnamed (C145).

records.title: S15 Create is unchanged; renumber skips a name taken by a non-regular entry or another writer by trying the next ID, and lint does not report non-regular entries
records.body: The S05 note: a directory or symlink named like the next record file is not a record file (C59), so the scan ignores it and Create gives up after three tries (C64). Renumber takes the next ID after a taken name instead (up to 10 tries), since it must finish a repair; changing Create belongs to the locking work (C114). Lint is about record files and ignores such entries.

records.title: S15 renumber picks new IDs that no link names without a file, and checks each move with the ID it will get
records.body: S15 review. A new ID equal to the target of an existing dangling link would silently make that link resolve to the moved record, so IDs named by a supersedes or superseded_by link with no file are skipped (one past the highest, then on until free). The in-memory check before the first write uses the same sequence, one ID per move, instead of one provisional ID for all, so a refusal changes nothing. Create had the same gap; C162 closed it (S23).

records.title: S15 an interrupted renumber's stale copy: renumber refuses (ErrStaleCopy, exit 1, nothing changed) and lint reports renumber-leftover; nothing is deleted automatically
records.body: S15 review of C148. After a crash between linking the new file and removing the old one, running renumber again would move the old file to yet another ID and the record would exist twice. A file is the stale copy when another file with a different ID and the same name text has a renumber history entry 'from N' for its ID at any position and holds the same record (C163). Renumber refuses when a colliding file is one, naming both files and saying to check both, then delete the old one; lint reports the old file as the error renumber-leftover, whether or not it still collides, so CI sees it. Deleting stays the owner's step: the tool cannot know the owner has not edited either file since.

records.title: S15 renumber syncs the store directory after linking the new file and before removing the old one, best effort
records.body: S15 review of C148. The file is synced, but the directory entry may not be on disk when the old name is removed; a crash could then lose both names. The directory sync closes that window. Errors are ignored because not every platform can sync a directory, and the effect cannot be observed in a test.

records.title: S15 renumber refuses a colliding record whose created is not a YYYY-MM-DD date
records.body: S15 review. The keeper is the record created first, compared as a date string (C146); a missing or malformed date would pick the keeper by accident of text order. The run stops with exit 1 naming the file and changes nothing; the owner fixes the date.

records.title: S23 lock file is <store>/.adj.lock, a persistent dot-file; adj writes no gitignore for it
records.body: Implementer decision (C32) for C114. The lock is taken on a file in the store directory (default decisions/.adj.lock), so it follows the store when the config moves it. The name starts with a dot, so the scan never takes it for a record (C59), and it is created on first use and never deleted: removing a lock file lets a waiting writer and a new one lock different files. It is empty. Tests and tools that list the store directory (names, tree, fileNames, TestRenumberLeavesNoTemporaryFiles) leave it out. Gitignore guidance: a team that does not want it in git adds <store>/.adj.lock (decisions/.adj.lock by default) to its .gitignore; committing the empty file is harmless. adj init and adj ask do not write or edit a .gitignore (out of the slice's scope), so the guidance is documented in AGENTS.md only.

records.title: S23 lock wait is bounded: LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB polled every 10 ms for up to 5 s, then an error naming the lock file
records.body: Implementer decision (C32) for C114. A blocking LOCK_EX would hang an agent's adj ask forever behind a hung process; a bounded wait fails instead. Create and Renumber try the flock without blocking, sleep 10 ms and try again until 5 s have passed, then return an error 'lock PATH: still held by another adj process after 5s; nothing was written' and write nothing (Create has not touched the directory beyond making it and the lock file; Renumber has read only). The flock goes with the file descriptor, so a process that dies releases it and no stale lock needs cleaning. Any other flock error (a file system without flock) is also an error naming the lock file. The timeout is a Store field in tests (lockTimeout), and lockBusy and beforeLink are the hooks tests use to hold one writer between scan and link; beforeLink now also runs before each Renumber link.

records.title: S23 flock builds on the systems that have syscall.Flock; every other system runs with no lock and the C64 retry
records.body: Implementer decision (C32) for C114. The slice proposed the unix build tag, but syscall.Flock does not exist on aix and solaris, which the unix tag includes (checked with go doc under GOOS=aix and GOOS=solaris; illumos has it), so the build would fail there. lock_unix.go is therefore tagged darwin || dragonfly || freebsd || illumos || linux || netbsd || openbsd, and lock_other.go (the negation) is the fallback: no lock, acquire returns a no-op. There Create keeps the bounded retry of C64, which catches two writers that choose the same file name, not two that choose the same ID with different names; lint and renumber find and fix those (C26). Windows is not locked (out of the slice). Cross-vetted with GOOS=windows, solaris and illumos to check it compiles; the fallback is not run by any test.

records.title: S23 Create and Renumber hold the lock; Renumber only when a collision exists; Create skips IDs named by dangling links
records.body: Implementer decision (C32) for C114, extending C155 and C154. Create validates the record with a stand-in ID before touching the store (a record that is invalid whatever its ID writes nothing, not even the directory or the lock file; one that is invalid only with its real ID fails after the lock made the directory and the lock file, so those exist but no record does), takes the lock, and holds it from the first scan to the link, retries included; it is validated again with the real ID. The ID is one past the highest, skipping any ID that a supersedes or superseded_by link names without a file (C155, as renumber does); a file that cannot be read keeps its ID by name but its links are unknown, so it is skipped for links rather than failing every ask. Renumber looks for collisions without the lock; with none it returns, taking no lock and making nothing. With one it takes the lock and reads the store again before it plans, and holds the lock to the last move (so a Create cannot take an ID a move is about to use). Update is not locked. Renumber that is refused after the lock leaves only the empty lock file.

records.title: S25 a stale copy must also hold the same record: IsStaleCopy compares the content, so a live record that shares the ID and name text with a moved one is not flagged
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C156. Name text plus a renumber entry 'from N' is not enough: two hand-named files with one ID and name text (0003-foo.md, 00003-foo.md) collide, one is moved to 0005-foo.md 'from 3', and the keeper 0003-foo.md then matched as its copy, so lint and renumber told the owner to delete a live record. IsStaleCopy(stale, staleRec, moved, movedRec) now also requires the same record, tested at a renumber entry 'from stale.ID' (any position in the history, as since S16). If that entry is the moved record's last, the moved record without it and with the stale ID must equal the stale record in every field and in the body. If entries follow it, the record was edited after the crash (adj decide or supersede, or by hand), so status, decision, rationale, links, body and so on may differ; it is then told apart from a keeper by what an edit cannot change: the history before the renumber entry must equal the stale record's whole history (an edit only appends), and title, key, tags, asked_by, created, context, options and recommendation (which only adj ask sets) must be equal. A keeper is another record, so its history or those fields differ. The record's id field is ignored on both sides (C59). The edited-since comparison covers the ask fields, not the body: body edits after the crash are allowed. Known limits: a moved file changed by hand without any history entry is no longer recognised and renumber would move it again, so before running renumber on duplicate-id files the owner checks whether one holds a renumber entry; and two files with identical records (contrived) leave the keeper flagged. Records are compared as stored (json of the frontmatter, body with its final newline), because the stale file may not be in the form Marshal writes (empty arrays, no final newline) while the moved file is. The reason for choosing this over a looser match is that a finding that tells the owner to delete a live record costs more than a missed leftover.

records.title: S25 the ID lock opens an existing read-only .adj.lock read-only when the read-write open fails with EACCES
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C114. flock needs no write access, so a lock file that exists but cannot be opened for writing (checked out of git by another user, chmod 444) must not stop every ask. acquire opens O_RDWR|O_CREATE as before; only on EACCES it opens the same path O_RDONLY (without O_CREATE, so only a file that exists) and flocks that. If the file is missing (a read-only directory) or the read-only open fails too, the error of the first open stands, so behaviour is as before; every other error is unchanged. The lock file is never written, so its mode and content stay. The lock still excludes: a second writer finds it held.

records.title: Release 0.1.0: an annotated v0.1.0 tag on local main; no remote, no push
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. adjudicate ships 0.1.0 once S26-S33 land. The release is an annotated git tag v0.1.0 on local main with a CHANGELOG.md entry. Publishing (creating a remote, pushing, go install from a module path) is a separate later step and needs the owner. The Later items S18-S22 stay later, after 0.1.0. Before the release: global flags before the subcommand, ask --ref, a free-text recommendation, decide --decided-at, adj amend, adj version, and PROJECT.md rewritten to match what shipped.

records.title: adj amend changes text fields only and records the old text in history
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. adj amend ID changes title, context, option tradeoffs, option summaries and rationale on a record of any status. It never changes status, the chosen option or decision, decided_by, asked_by, dates, ID, links, key or tags. Each amend appends a dated history entry (a new event) that keeps the old text of every changed field, so the record shows what it said before. Flag names and the history note format are the implementer's call (C32).

records.title: A free-text recommendation: ask --recommend-text
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. ask --recommend-text TEXT records a recommendation that is not one of the options (it has no option label). inbox, show and check display it, and the owner accepts it with decide ID --text as today. --recommend and --recommend-text are exclusive. The JSON shape gets a documented field for it (docs/json.md). The field name and storage are the implementer's call (C32).

records.title: decide --decided-at DATE backdates a decision and keeps the run date in history
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. adj decide takes --decided-at YYYY-MM-DD. decided_at is set to the given date. The history entry keeps the real run date, so backdating stays visible. A date after the run date is refused with a usage error. Other validation (for example a date before the record's created date) is the implementer's call (C32).

records.title: adj version and --version report the version from build info, with an ldflags override
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. adj version and adj --version print the version. It comes from runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo (the module version when the binary is built by go install module@version), and a package variable set with -ldflags -X overrides it for local release builds. A plain local build prints (devel) or the VCS revision the build info carries. Standard library only.

records.title: adj --root: given twice is a usage error (S26, C32)
records.body: A --root before the command and another after it is a usage error (exit 2) naming both values, and so is --root twice before the command. Reason: silently taking the later one would hide a mistake that points a write at the wrong store. --root twice after the command keeps taking the last (unchanged). A leading --root with --help/-h prints the main usage (exit 0); with no command or no value it exits 2; before ai it exits 2 (ai takes no --root) unless ai is given --help, which is handled first and exits 0 (as adj ai --help --root D does).

records.title: S28: a free-text recommendation is the recommendation's text key; label and text are exclusive
records.body: Recommendation gains Text (JSON text, omitempty); Label becomes omitempty so existing records write the same bytes. Validate accepts text alone, still rejects a label that is not an option, and rejects label with text, blank text, or neither. Reason: the smallest change that keeps old files identical and leaves IsStaleCopy comparing the whole recommendation.

records.title: S28: --recommend-text is kept as typed and shown on the Recommendation line
records.body: Like decide --text and --reasoning, the text is stored as typed and only a blank one exits 2. show and inbox print it after 'Recommendation:' in place of the label (a multi-line text goes under the label, as for other fields). adj check text output is unchanged (an open record has no detail lines, C106); check --json carries the record, text included. Reason: no new wording to learn, parity with how a label recommendation already shows. Owner confirmed 2026-10-17: check text stays as built; C106 stands.

records.title: S28: the agent snippet names --recommend-text in one sentence
records.body: internal/commands/ai.md says 'No option fits? Use --recommend-text "Text".', drops the '(also --tag T, --format json)' aside on the context line, and (after the merge with S27) shortens the --ref sentence to 'Repeat --ref ID for slice or catalog references.' (the word 'opaque' dropped; AGENTS.md still says refs are opaque strings), to stay under the 1800-byte cap (C125). Reason: the friction came from agents that had no option to recommend.

records.title: Ask refs in search and active views
records.body: adj check searches refs, and inbox/check text shows them so owners see linked slice or catalog context on open records and ref-based matches.

records.title: S29 permits decided_at before created
records.body: Allow --decided-at before created because S17 records decisions entered days after they were made; created marks when the record was logged.

records.title: S29 labels a backdated decide history entry
records.body: When --decided-at differs from the run date, set the decide history note to backdated to YYYY-MM-DD so the run date remains visible beside the effective date.

records.title: S30 adj amend flags: --title, --context or --stdin, --summary LABEL:TEXT, --tradeoffs LABEL:TEXT and --rationale, any number in one call
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C166. Flag names follow the existing ones: --context/--stdin as on ask, LABEL:TEXT split at the first colon as ask's --option and --tradeoffs (the label is trimmed and each label once per flag), --rationale for the field C166 names (not --why, which would read as the reason for the amend). One call may change several fields and still appends one history entry. Texts are kept as typed (title, context, rationale) or trimmed (option summary and tradeoffs, as ask does). Blank values follow ask and decide: a blank --title, --context or --rationale, a multi-line title, a malformed or repeated LABEL:TEXT and a call with no field are usage errors (exit 2) before the store is looked for; an empty TEXT in --summary or --tradeoffs clears that option text (both are optional on ask), but a context cannot be emptied. A label that no option has is a usage error too, which also covers 'renaming' an option: no flag changes a label. Reason: stay close to ask/decide so the CLI has one vocabulary, and keep every refusal before any write.

records.title: S30 an amend history entry is the event amend with a note naming the changed fields and a was object holding their old text
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C166. A new HistoryEntry key was (omitted when absent, allowed on amend entries only, and required there) holds one entry per changed field: title, context, rationale as strings and options as [{label, summary?, tradeoffs?}] in the record's option order. A field the call left alone, or gave its current text, is not in it; an old empty text is kept as an empty string (a pointer in Go), so 'was empty' is told apart from 'not changed'. note is the list of changed fields in a fixed order (title, context, per option summary then tradeoffs, rationale). Validate checks the shape, so lint reports a broken entry as a fields finding. adj show prints each old text under the entry as 'was FIELD: text' (multi-line text indented under its label, an empty old text as (empty)). Reason: a structured value can be rolled back by IsStaleCopy (C181) and read by agents in show --json; a free-text note could not be, and the old text of a multi-line field would have to be parsed back out of prose.

records.title: S30 adj amend errors: a rationale on an open record and an amend that changes nothing exit 1, bad arguments and a label that no option has exit 2, and a title change does not rename the file
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C166 and the slice's failing tests. Exit 1 (a failed operation, C34) when the arguments are fine but the record cannot take them: an unknown or duplicate ID, a --rationale on an open record (it has none; the whole call is refused, a title given beside it is not written), and an amend whose texts all equal what the record says ('nothing to change'). A text equal to the current one beside a real change is simply left out of the entry. Exit 2 for what is wrong with the arguments whatever the record is, or with a label against the record's options (as decide's OPTION is). Everything is validated in memory before the one store.Update, so a refusal writes nothing. store.Update keeps the file name, so an amended title leaves the slug of the file as it was (the same as before any amend: a file is named once, at ask), which also keeps IsStaleCopy's name-text test valid. Reason: the same split between usage and failure the other commands use; no rename keeps links and git history of the file stable.

records.title: S30 IsStaleCopy takes each amend entry after the renumber entry back to its old text before comparing the fields adj ask sets
records.body: Implementer decision (C32), refining C163. adj amend can now change the title, context and option summary/tradeoffs that C163 treated as set only by adj ask, so an edited-since moved record legitimately differs from its stale file there. Options weighed: (1) leave those fields out of the comparison, which is simple but lets a keeper that an amend made look like the stale record (or the reverse) be flagged, and the title/context/options are most of what tells two records of one day and one name text apart; (2) roll the amend entries after the renumber entry back (newest first, using the old text they keep) and compare the result to the stale record, which keeps the check as strong as before. Chosen (2). The history before the renumber entry must still equal the stale record's whole history, compared by content because an amend entry holds pointers; key, tags, asked_by, created, option labels and the recommendation, which no amend changes, are compared as they are; an amend entry that names an option the record does not have fails the match; an amend before the renumber entry is part of the common history and is not rolled back; the rationale is not among the compared fields. The C163 known limits stay (a hand edit with no history entry is not recognised). A finding that tells the owner to delete a live record still costs more than a missed leftover.

records.title: Local version output includes VCS revision
records.body: When the module version is (devel), append the available VCS revision after it on the same output line so local builds identify both their development status and source revision.

records.title: Who may amend: agents amend open records only; the owner amends decided records
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-17. Agents may amend the title, context and option summaries/tradeoffs of open records; only the owner amends a decided record, rationale included. Guidance for agents (AGENTS.md, adj ai), not enforced in code, like C27. The owner also accepted the S30 amend UX as built (C178, C180): a context cannot be emptied, an empty TEXT clears an option field, and a title change does not rename the file.

records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-18 (S34). records.title: adj context --max-bytes: selection and output
records.body: Implementer decisions under C32 (S35), confirmed by the owner 2026-10-18. Newest = decided_at descending, then ID descending; the kept records are the largest newest-first prefix that fits, printed in ID order. N counts every byte written (md omitted line included; the whole JSON document). md ends with a blank line then 'N decisions omitted' ('1 decision omitted'), only when something was omitted. JSON gets an integer 'omitted' key (0 included) only when --max-bytes is given; without the flag output is byte-identical to 0.1.0. Nothing fits: md prints only the omitted line, JSON {"decisions": [], "omitted": N}, exit 0; if even that exceeds N, empty stdout and exit 1 naming the budget and bytes needed. The value is a whole number >= 1, trimmed; 0, negative, blank, non-numeric, fractional or overflow exits 2 before store access; repeated, the last counts. The key is documented in its own docs/json.md section.

records.title: Slicer integration: --ref filter on list and context
records.body: Owner decision 2026-10-18 (S20). The adj side of the slicer integration is a --ref filter on adj list and adj context: exact match against a record's refs, repeatable, every --ref given must be among the record's refs, plus a documented recipe (adj list --ref S20 --json). No slicer-side change and no dependency either way (C12).

records.title: --ref filter values are matched as typed
records.body: Implementer decision under C32 (S20). --ref values on adj list and adj context match exact, case-sensitive values as typed, with no trimming, because refs are opaque strings stored as typed; a blank or whitespace-only value exits 2 before store access.
